title: Review: reading my first words
topic: review of the letters ש ל מ ם ה ו א ב ת י נ ן ד ר and the vowels
why: Review of the first unit: no new letters; you reread the twelve letters (and their two final forms), all the vowels and the shva in words and short sentences. By the end, you should be able to decode a simple sentence on your own before tackling the rest of the alef-bet.

{"lessons": ["

Your twelve letters

Well done: you already know twelve letters (and two final forms). Read them again out loud, from right to left.

LetterNameSound
שׁshinsh
לlamedl
מ םmem, final memm
הhelight h, silent at the end of a word
וvavv, o (וֹ) or u (וּ)
אalefsilent
בּ בbet, vetb with the dot, v without the dot
תtavt
יyody, or i after a hiriq
נ ןnun, final nunn
דdaletd
רreshr (from the throat)

The final forms ם and ן are only used at the end of a word: שָׁלוֹם, לָבָן.

", "

All the vowels

MarkSoundExample
מָ מַ (kamats, patah)a (as in father)שָׁלוֹם shalom
נֵ דֶ (tsere, segol)e (as in bed)דֶּלֶת delet
מִ (hiriq)i (as in see)מִי mi
וֹ לֹ (holam)o (as in more)לֹא lo
וּ בֻ (shuruk, kubutz)u (as in food)בֻּבָּה buba
תְ (shva)nothing, or a very short eתְּמוּנָה tmuna
אֲ (hataf patah)short aאֲנִי ani

The holam (o) goes on a vav, וֹ, or on its own, at the top left of the letter: לֹא is read lo.

A vowel is always read AFTER the letter that carries it: מִ = mi, never \"im\".

", "

Reading whole sentences

For a long word, break it into syllables: a letter and its vowel, then the next one.

תְּ־מוּ־נָהt-mu-na: tmuna, a photo
מִי בַּתְּמוּנָה?Who is in the photo? [mi ba-tmuna?]
הִנֵּה אַבָּא, וְהִנֵּה אִמָּא.Here's Dad, and here's Mom. [hine aba, ve-hine ima]
דּוֹד רוֹן מוֹרֶה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם.Uncle Ron is a teacher in Jerusalem. [dod Ron more birushalayim]

You can also introduce yourself (אֲנִי דָּנָה), answer (נָעִים מְאוֹד, with a silent ע that you'll study soon; כֵּן is also a word to recognize) and say who is where, without the verb \"to be\".

הִנֵּה (hine, here is) is used to show something or someone, pointing at it with your finger.
